title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Pond and water-feature maintenance
audience: Solo operators and team owners of pond and water-feature maintenance businesses who want repeat bookings and referrals from clients they have already served.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask at the moment the client is most satisfied
instruction.body: The best time to ask for a review or referral is after the client has confirmed the pond is working as agreed, usually at sign-off or when the invoice is paid. Ask in one sentence, name the next step you would like, such as a review or the name of one person with a water feature, and make it easy to decline. Record what you asked and what the client said. Timing matters: in one Baylor Keller Center experiment, a late reminder brought in more reviews than an immediate one (1 June 2024). It was one experiment only. The AMA says timing should match the product, because experience goods need more evaluation time (10 January 2023). Google lets a business share a review link or QR code (Google Business Profile Help). Do not write reviews for clients or invent them. Asking only the happy clients is called review gating, and Podium, a vendor, says Google treats it as a violation (2 May 2022; not checked against Google's policy). Incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (ACCC, 15 July 2026). Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews, so check each platform's terms before offering any incentive.

instruction.heading: Offer the next service before the client leaves
instruction.body: At sign-off, propose the next step with a date: a routine visit that continues, a filter or pump service, or a clean-out before a season the owner has told you about. Put the scope, the interval and the price approach in writing, and confirm that the client agrees before you change their schedule. The research found no pond-specific interval or retention figure, so choose the interval from your own visit records and test it. Housecall Pro, a vendor, recommends a short follow-up after each completed job about the maintenance plan (8 June 2026). If the written offer goes by email or text, check the electronic message rules first. ACMA's guidance says inferred consent is narrow and does not cover a message sent just after a purchase.

instruction.heading: Check in at the interval that suits the service
instruction.body: The research found no pond-specific check-in interval, so the interval is a choice to test. Choose one from your own records, such as the next scheduled visit or a set number of weeks after a repair. The check asks whether the water and pump are still working, whether anything has changed, such as new plants, a new fish stock or an overflow after rain, and whether there is other work to quote. Keep it short, record what the client said, and close the loop with a reply. A check-in that only asks about the result may not be commercial, but a message that promotes any service can be, even when it is framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, 9 November 2023). ACMA's guidance requires an unsubscribe option on every commercial message.

instruction.heading: Re-contact previous clients before their busy periods
instruction.body: No pond-specific busy period was confirmed in the research, so choose the periods from your own service history. Plan a short message a few weeks before each period, and offer slots you can actually deliver, with a clear way to opt out. Do not use the message to pressure anyone, and do not contact a client who has asked not to hear from you. ACMA says an unsubscribe must be honoured within five working days, so record each opt-out as soon as you receive it. At the end of the period, review the response and note which timing worked.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: A referral reward works best when the client knows the terms before they refer someone. Decide what you will offer, such as a credit on the next visit or a small thank-you, and write down the condition for payment, which is normally that the referred person has completed a paid job. Research on referral programmes found that stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals in the studies reported (Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research, 2023). Get the referred person's consent before any referral message is sent, because the referrer's word alone may not be enough (Clayton Utz, 11 May 2017). Check any cash-based reward, and its tax or contract effect, with an adviser before you start. No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found, so those points remain unconfirmed. Retailers are a possible partner for a referral arrangement. Queensland's fact sheet says unwanted fish should go back to the retailer, be rehomed, or be humanely destroyed. That is a reason to ask a retailer whether it will take fish, not a confirmed referral channel. Set any reward for a retailer in writing too, and check it against each platform's and each retailer's own rules.

procedure: After each job is signed off, make one review or referral request and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-service offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and confirm it with the client.
Schedule the check-in for an interval you have chosen from your own records, and send it using the electronic message rules.
Plan a re-contact message for each busy period in your own calendar, and exclude anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books, confirm the referred job is paid before applying the reward, and record the outcome.
Review at the end of each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: A pond owner's koi must be rehomed after a liner repair. The business suggests a retailer that has agreed to take fish. The retailer asks whether the business will send customers it refers to the shop.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the business write down before any referral happens, and what should it avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: The business writes down any arrangement with the retailer before a referral: what each party does, the condition for any payment, and how the fish handover is recorded. It does not promise a reward it has not written down. It does not release any fish into a waterway or drain, because the state rule forbids it. It asks the koi owner whether the owner agrees to be passed to the retailer, and it contacts the owner only if the owner says yes. If the reward has any tax or contract effect, the business confirms it with an adviser before the arrangement starts.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-service offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of re-contact dates chosen from the business's own service history
Written referral reward terms, including any retailer arrangement
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the client has confirmed the result.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after sign-off or payment, when the client has confirmed the result is right.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so the terms are disputed later.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral is made, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing a client's name, photo or review without their consent for that use.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a client who asked not to hear from you, or using a re-contact message to pressure them.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list, honour it at once, and keep re-contact messages factual and optional.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a client's name, photo, review or property detail needs the client's consent for that use. Do not write reviews on a client's behalf or invent them. If the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business, client details are also personal information. The OAIC's guidelines (13 May 2026) say the Act covers organisations above a turnover threshold and some others, so check whether it applies to you.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on the review's content. Check each platform's rules before offering any reward.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a service reminder, so check each message before sending.

Fish must not be released into waterways, wetlands or drains, and rules differ by state. In New South Wales, releasing fish into public waters without a permit is illegal. In Victoria, koi need a permit to keep, transport or possess. Any referral that involves fish must follow the rule for the state where the pond is.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-service offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the client before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-service offers with the date, scope, interval and client confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the client has confirmed the result, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next service in writing, with a date, before the client leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a pond client for a review or referral?
options: Before the job starts, so the client feels committed
After the client has confirmed the result is right
Only when the client has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A client wants to publish a review with their name and a photo of the finished pond work. What do you need?
options: Their consent for the name and photo you plan to publish
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred person books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the condition for payment stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say to propose the next step for a pond client?
options: At the end of each job, with a date

sourceReferences: Google Business Profile Help, 'Review links', https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122?hl=en-GB, no date shown. Supports: a business may share a review link or QR code; discounts or goods in exchange for reviews are banned.

ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026. Supports: incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on the review's content.

Baylor Keller Center, 'Wait Just a Minute', https://kellercenter.hankamer.baylor.edu/news/story/2024/wait-just-minute-when-ask-online-reviews, 1 June 2024 (metadata says 13 May 2024). One experiment only. Supports: a later reminder brought in more reviews than an immediate one.

AMA, 'Asking for customer reviews at the right time', https://www.ama.org/2023/01/10/asking-for-customer-reviews-at-the-right-time-sooner-is-not-always-better/, 10 January 2023. Supports: timing should match the product type.
Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; the Google position it describes was not checked against Google's policy.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Supports: stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals. No figures used.

Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017 (older than 2022). Supports: the referred person's consent before a referral message.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023. Supports: a reminder that promotes any service can be commercial.

ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown; read 2026-11-04. Supports: consent for marketing messages; unsubscribe honoured within five working days; inferred consent is narrow.

Housecall Pro, 'Recurring service agreements', https://www.housecallpro.com/resources/recurring-service-agreements/, 8 June 2026 (updated 9 June 2026). Vendor source. Supports: a short follow-up after each completed job about the maintenance plan.

Queensland Department of Agriculture and Fisheries, 'Ipa aquarium fish importation' fact sheet, https://www.daf.qld.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0004/1457824/ipa-aquarium-fish-importation.pdf, dated June 2020. Supports: unwanted fish should go back to the retailer, be rehomed, or be humanely destroyed; fish must not be released.

NSW DPI, 'Freshwater pest fish in NSW', Primefact 1336, https://www.dpi.nsw.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0010/637129/Primefact-1336-Freshwater-pest-fish-in-NSW.pdf, September 2023. Supports: releasing fish into NSW public waters without a permit is illegal.

Victorian Fisheries Authority, 'Noxious aquatic species in Victoria', https://vfa.vic.gov.au/operational-policy/pests-and-diseases/noxious-aquatic-species-in-victoria, undated. Supports: koi carp need a permit to keep, transport or possess.

Gap: no pond-specific repeat-service, retention or referral figure was found. No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found. The retailer referral route is an inference from the Queensland fact sheet and is not a confirmed channel.

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam (ACMA)
officialReferences.covers: Says commercial messages cannot be sent without the recipient's permission or consent; messages must accurately identify the sender and include correct contact details; every commercial message must contain an unsubscribe option. Does not mention one-to-one messages. Publisher: ACMA.
